key_insight: VLA Foundry provides a single open-source training stack that unifies language, vision-language, and action model training, enabling end-to-end control from pretraining to action fine-tuning in one codebase.
problem_solved: Fragmented and incompatible VLA toolchains that force researchers to stitch together separate pretraining and action-training pipelines, hindering reproducibility, extensibility, and end-to-end experimentation.
method: Unified codebase that integrates LLM, VLM, and VLA training stages into a shared training stack with end-to-end control.
Support for both from-scratch training and using pretrained backbones (e.g., Hugging Face), enabling flexible initialization and rapid prototyping.
Modular pipelines for language pretraining → vision-language alignment → action-expert fine-tuning, packaged as an open-source framework for reproducible workflows.
impact: Simplifies engineering overhead and reproducibility for multimodal action research, accelerating iteration on VLA models and enabling consistent comparisons across training regimes.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing stages: Language pretraining → Vision-language alignment → Action fine-tuning (single unified codebase)

paper_title: VLA Foundry: A Unified Framework for Training Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_authors: Jean Mercat, Sedrick Keh, Kushal Arora, Isabella Huang, Paarth Shah
